text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The central bank expects full liberalisation of capital account transactions by the end of 2001. The last move toward full liberalisation should be permission for foreigners to buy real estate in Slovakia.
- President Michal Kovac begins an official two-day visit to Netherlands. On Tuesday Kovac will addresss the Dutch parliament and meet Prime Minister Vim Kok.
- Commercial banks said a new central bank measure on foreign exchange positions will, in the long-term perspective, slowdown the inflow of foreign financial resoures.

- Bankers said the measure, aimed at reducing loans in hard currencies, may prove to be ineffective since the central bank can still approve direct foreign credit and this will increase overall volume of the hard currency loans.

- Max van der Stoel, high commissioner for minorities of the Organisation for Cooperation and Security and Europe (OSCE), said Slovakia still needed to solve the question of the law on the use of minority languages in official relations.
- The government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda includes discussion on the final draft of the state budget for 1997.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Hard currency revenue from tourism totalled $469 million in the first eight months of the year, compared with the $445.6 million for the whole of 1995.

- The overall volume of loans totalled 355.4 billion crowns as of September 30. Loans extended in Slovak crowns totalled 315.3 billion crowns. Loans extended in hard currencies represented a sum of 40.1 billion crowns.
- Slovakia's largest cellulose and paper producer SCP Ruzomberok will issue an unspecified tranche of bonds, the company's extraordinary shareholders meeting ruled on Monday.

- The National Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, approved another 24 privatisations, of which the largest sale was a 67 percent stake in the chemical company Istrochem a.s. for 1.8 billion crowns.
- The British supermarket network Tesco, which bought several stores in Slovakia from the U.S. Kmart, can not import British food as this does not meet the Slovak veterinary requirements.

- About 38 percent of Slovak construction companies said their production increased in October from the September level, a poll by the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said. Some 50 percent of those polled companies said they expected a decline in production over the next three moths.
- The state-owned public transport company SAD s.p. needs at least 100 million crowns to prevent an iminent collapse.

PRAVDA - Deputy Finance Minister Jozef Magula, known for his involvement in liquidation of several Slovak investment funds, has proposed his resignation in a protest against the recently approved amendment to securitiies law, which he said will hurt transparency of the capital market.
